items.q: Match the Type 1.5 form to its gender entry — 1) Ketosis-prone/Flatbush diabetes 2) Latent autoimmune diabetes of adults … A) m > F B) m = F
items.exp: The table gives m > F for ketosis-prone/Flatbush diabetes and m = F for latent autoimmune diabetes of adults. (Book p921)

items.q: The ketosis-prone/Flatbush course begins at approximately what age in the table?
items.exp: The KPD/Flatbush course is written as early age, approximately 20 years, with ketosis. (Book p921)

items.q: A person is asymptomatic, is accidentally found hyperglycemic at about 30 years, and is initially treated as Type 2 DM without insulin. Which Type 1.5 form matches the table?
items.exp: The LADA column describes an asymptomatic patient around 30 years found hyperglycemic and treated as Type 2 DM without insulin. (Book p921)

items.q: Assess the Type 1.5 course: I KPD shows reduced insulin requirement after 5–10 years. II LADA shows increased insulin requirement after 5–10 years.
items.exp: The table shows reduced insulin requirement after 5–10 years for KPD and increased insulin requirement after 5–10 years for LADA. (Book p921)

items.q: After the early ketosis phase, KPD is followed by decreased insulin requirement, ___ and good response to oral hypoglycemic agents.
items.exp: The KPD course arrow points to obesity and then good response to OHA after decreased insulin requirement. (Book p921)

items.q: Match the LADA table feature to its entry — 1) C-peptide value 2) Antibody level 3) Presentation 4) Clinical build … A) Slightly decreased, slower than T1DM B) Increased markedly C) T1DM behaves like T2DM D) Lean, fair with autoimmune illness stigmata
items.exp: The LADA column gives slightly decreased C-peptide, markedly increased antibodies, T1DM behaving like T2DM, and a lean fair patient with autoimmune stigmata. (Book p921)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the KPD clinical features written in the table?
items.exp: KPD is described with a dark, hirsute, obese male, acanthosis nigricans/balanoposthitis and hyperinsulinemia; lean fair build belongs to the LADA column. (Book p921)

items.q: The table says that one third of diagnosed Type 2 DM cases are in reality:
items.exp: The clinical-features row states that one third of diagnosed Type 2 DM cases are in reality LADA. (Book p921)

items.q: Match each antibody to the table's sensitivity — 1) GAD 2) ICA 3) IAA 4) ZnT8 … A) 70–90% B) 44–100% C) 40–70% D) 50–70%
items.exp: The antibody table lists sensitivities of GAD 70–90%, ICA 44–100%, IAA 40–70% and ZnT8 50–70%. (Book p921)

items.q: Which antibody specificity is written for GAD in the table?
items.exp: The GAD row gives 99% specificity. (Book p921)

items.q: Assess the antibody notes: I ICA is described as earliest to appear and disappears after a few years. II IAA is described as invalid after therapy and common in new-onset T1DM.
items.exp: Both antibody rows carry those exact additional features in the table. (Book p921)

items.q: For a young patient in the algorithm with low fasting C-peptide and positive antibodies, which label does the page's flowchart give?
items.exp: The printed diagnostic algorithm maps low fasting C-peptide with positive antibodies to LADA. (Book p921)
